A_trait: bird-flower access/reward syndrome; natural floral phenotype
decision_note: Primary Isoplexis study experimentally demonstrates effective bird pollination and records insect nectar thieves/secondary robbers on the same flowers. Floral phenotype itself is not manipulated as one shared causal coordinate, so retain as near-pass.

A_trait: petal length; fruit size; mericarp spines across island and continental populations
decision_note: Primary Tribulus comparative study documents island-continent divergence in floral traits associated with pollination and fruit-defense traits associated with vertebrate granivory. It is evolutionary-outcome evidence, not a matched two-function response geometry.
bioRxiv preprint of the pollen-dispensing study published as SCHPRISMA-000622 / American Journal of Botany DOI 10.1002/ajb2.1680; exclude duplicate report and retain version of record.

A_trait: poricidal anther morphology; anther wall area; pore size
decision_note: Primary Solanum study links anther morphology to pollen dispensing under bee-like vibration. Pollinating bees are also pollen consumers, creating a service-cost role boundary, but no common plant reproductive endpoint closes a strict H1 geometry.
